newsitem.title: UK: Man charged over IRA attack at Belfast court.
newsitem.headline: Man charged over IRA attack at Belfast court.

text.p: A 27-year-old Belfast man was charged on Saturday over an IRA rocket attack earlier this week on a security post at Northern Ireland's law courts.

Brendan Hugh McIlvenny was charged in court with conspiring to murder members of the security forces and was ordered to be held in custody for three weeks. His lawyer told the court he would be pleading not guilty.
A police officer was slightly hurt on Monday when the Irish Republican Army fired a missile at a security hut at the entrance to the courts.

It was the latest in a spate of attacks and botched raids by the IRA which have prompted fears Northern Ireland could slide back into a cycle of sectarian warfare that scarred it for 27 years until twin truces by Republican and Protestant guerrillas.

The IRA, fighting a war to end British rule of Northern Ireland, abandoned a 17-month truce in February last year. Britain says the IRA must reinstate the truce before its Sinn Fein political wing is given a seat in all-party talks on the province's future.
